title: Level up your legs
summary: A long talk on building big legs: why big glutes and legs are not feminine and do not thicken a natural's waist, why to train hip hinges and knee flexions often but minimally, and why cardio does not kill leg gains. He also covers mobility through full range lifting, leg extensions and curls as complements only, and unilateral work.
claims: Wanting small legs is a valid aesthetic choice; you get to build the body you prefer
Avoid hybrid lifts like squats ending in a calf raise or knee raise; balancing at the top of a heavy lift is dangerous
His dream physique has legs so big they become upsetting
Big glutes cannot hurt a male physique: they are not visible from the front and are separated from the upper back by a slimmer lower back, and roundness is prized in bodybuilding
Male glutes are square and store little fat, so growing them will not look feminine; only guys who do nothing but squats end up disproportionate
Weak glutes cause round-back deadlifts and good-morning squats; the glutes keep you erect under load
Isolating glutes is a meme for most men; squats and deadlifts build them, and hip thrusts only emphasize rather than isolate
At any powerlifting meet, natural lifters who do compounds all have big glutes
Big male legs are not feminine: they are square, leaner and hairy, nothing like a female leg
The frog physique, a big lower body with little else, is common in powerlifters and strength trainees
Compound leg training does not thicken a natural's waist; that is an enhanced effect of GH and insulin. His waist looks better now than at 17 because he added muscle
He prefers big legs and an X taper over the slimmer legs of the 70s and 80s
His standards: 20-22 inch thighs are small, 26-27 inches big, 29-30 inches very big
The best way to prevent lower back injuries is to deadlift and knee injuries to squat; someone who deadlifts 400 lb will not hurt his back picking something up
Muscle built through a lifetime of lifting is carried into old age; the most mobile old people he knows always lifted
A natural's legs peak in his mid 30s and keep growing year after year; he has never had his legs plateau in size
Big legs make shopping for jeans hard; buy stretchy elastic jeans
Big legs get noticed and complimented more than the upper body because few people, even gym bros, develop them
Build big legs with hip hinges and knee flexions of any kind; you can grow huge legs without squats or deadlifts but never without a knee flexion and a hip hinge
People skip legs because training them once a week causes brutal soreness; frequency is king, train legs every two days or every other session
The SS pitfall: novice and powerlifting programs squat and deadlift too often; lower body days should be shorter than upper days because they move more tonnage
Minimalism is ideal for lower body: pick one knee flexion and one hip hinge, do them once or twice a week, and add variations
He has never had a leg pump in his life, yet built 26.5-inch thighs
To maintain leg size: train legs once a week with a little strength work, or squat and deadlift every 15 days and do cardio the rest of the time
Size and function do not correlate unless function dictates size, as in powerlifting; maximizing size sacrifices some function
Cardio does not kill leg gains: biking 30 minutes to and from the gym did not reduce his squat or deadlift or slow his recovery
Low intensity cardio barely touches heavy lifters' recovery, but heavy leg training can hurt endurance performance, so fighters and athletes must program legs carefully
Getting winded on squats and deadlifts means a weak cardiovascular system; he can squat 8 reps to failure without breathing hard
Build lifting endurance with higher-rep squats and deadlifts or high-intensity cardio; once built, cardio endurance is easy to maintain
Mobility comes from lifting through full range with manageable weight and pristine form, not from stretching and foam rolling
Depth depends on limb length, so do not force it; partials are fine but always keep at least one full range leg lift in the program
Leg extensions have no carryover to the squat; they can complement squats but never replace them, and he usually cuts them from programs as junk volume
Trying to isolate every muscle head with machines is a pro bodybuilder complication; for naturals a compound knee flexion covers most of the leg
Leg curls without a hip hinge waste time; after deadlifts they complement the hinge by working the stretch and preventing injury
The lower back, not the knee, is the most common injury in squats and deadlifts, from bad technique and too much frequency
Keep leg exercise selection and frequency minimal to stay healthy: someone consistent for five years ends up bigger than someone who goes all out for one
Lower back pain the day after deadlifts is not DOMS to be proud of; it means you are not pulling with your legs
He hates unilateral work after countless lunge laps in football, but lunges are good for unloading the lower back and suit people who want slimmer, athletic legs
Athleticism means function in a sport, not lean separated looks; a sumo wrestler's legs are athletic too
exercises: Squat with calf raise or knee raise
dangerous hybrid; balancing at the top of a heavy lift
emphasizes glutes but does not isolate them; optional for most men
no carryover; junk volume if it replaces knee flexion
stretch work that complements deadlifts and prevents injury
unloads lower back; staggered stance is more athletic
